pr_title: origin/master if no base is defined for create pr

issue_context.title: `gh pr create` attempts to lookup commits from local `master`
issue_context.body:
### Describe the bug

When attempting to create a pr from a repo without a local `master` branch `github pr create` fails to compute title/body defaults (and presumable gets the wrong commits if local `master` != upstream `master`).

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

```console
> git clone https://github.com/Nemo157/cbor.nemo157.com
Cloning into 'cbor.nemo157.com'...
remote: Enumerating objects: 26, done.
remote: Counting objects: 100% (26/26), done.
remote: Compressing objects: 100% (26/26), done.
remote: Total 734 (delta 10), reused 4 (delta 0), pack-reused 708
Receiving objects: 100% (734/734), 2.77 MiB | 3.54 MiB/s, done.
Resolving deltas: 100% (497/497), done.
> cd cbor.nemo157.com
> git checkout -b foo
Switched to a new branch 'foo'
> git branch -d master
Deleted branch master (was b9d93eb).
> gh pr create

Creating pull request for foo into master in Nemo157/cbor.nemo157.com

! warning: could not compute title or body defaults: fatal: ambiguous argument 'master...foo': unknown revision or path not in the working tree.
Use '--' to separate paths from revisions, like this:
'git <command> [<revision>...] -- [<file>...]'
git: exit status 128
? Title
```

### Expected vs actual behavior

The remote branch should be used for computing the appropriate commits to use (`origin/master...foo` in the example above).

### Logs

```console
> gh --version
gh version 0.6.2 (2020-03-18)
https://github.com/cli/cli/releases/tag/v0.6.2
```
comments:
Thank you for reporting!

> The remote branch should be used for computing the appropriate commits to use (`origin/master...foo` in the example above).

Completely agreed. We could also use the latest commit hash for `origin/master` that we can easily obtain by querying the API 👍

@mislav I'm on `0.6.4` but seem to still be running into this 🤔

```sh
gh pr create

Creating pull request for master into master in Homebrew/homebrew-cask-drivers

! warning: could not compute title or body defaults: fatal: ambiguous argument 'upstream/master...master': unknown revision or path not in the working tree.
Use '--' to separate paths from revisions, like this:
'git <command> [<revision>...] -- [<file>...]'
git: exit status 128
? Title
```

@lumaxis Thank you for reporting.
```
Creating pull request for master into master in Homebrew/homebrew-cask-drivers
```
Was your current branch `master` when you were running `pr create`?
@mislav Yes! And just to note, creating the PR actually worked in the end, it just didn’t suggest a title or body.

Also, in case that helps, I set up the local repo with `gh repo fork`:
```sh
$ gh repo fork https://github.com/Homebrew/homebrew-cask-drivers
- Forking Homebrew/homebrew-cask-drivers...
✓ Created fork lumaxis/homebrew-cask-drivers
? Would you like to clone the fork? Yes
Cloning into 'homebrew-cask-drivers'...
remote: Enumerating objects: 58, done.
remote: Counting objects: 100% (58/58), done.
remote: Compressing objects: 100% (44/44), done.
remote: Total 6907 (delta 35), reused 19 (delta 14), pack-reused 6849
Receiving objects: 100% (6907/6907), 1.14 MiB | 2.28 MiB/s, done.
Resolving deltas: 100% (4713/4713), done.
✓ Cloned fork
```
Then edited on the `master` branch, committed, ran `gh pr create`.

review_comments: The `Comits()` method is not used anywhere thats why I thought to modify the signature and implementation. From the title of the method I think It can be used in other places in the future. In that case the whole thing can be done in the `computeDefaults` method. Thanks!
